newsitem.title: JAPAN: NTT urges U.S. FCC to reconsider licence delay.
newsitem.headline: NTT urges U.S. FCC to reconsider licence delay.

text.p: Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp said on Wednesday it had written to the U.S. Federal Communications Commission urging it to quickly grant NTT a U.S. international phone licence.
NTT said the issue of its procurement, cited by the FCC as a reason for delaying the licence, were irrelevant to the application.
"We hope the U.S. will grant the licence quickly in accordance with the spirit of the telecom pact under the World Trade Organisation," NTT said in the letter.

Earlier this month, U.S. regulators told NTT and Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co (KDD) that they had put on hold their applications to offer international long-distance phone services so that the Clinton administration could review them for trade concerns.
The FCC said the U.S. Trade Representative's (USTR) office, the Commerce Department and State Department had told the FCC that the applications "may raise trade policy concerns".
The USTR has urged Japan to renew NTT's procurement pact and to scrap a 20 percent ceiling on foreign ownership in NTT and KDD.
The procurement pact, which sets guidelines for NTT's international purchases of equipment, expires in September.
KDD said it has also sent a similar letter to the FCC.
